topics.title: Fowler meets Ausable: a disappointing secret agent
topics.ncert_sections: Opening of the story (up to 'In that thought is drama')

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Ausable's appearance, accent and surroundings differ from the usual image of a secret agent.
Explain why Fowler, a young romantic writer, feels let down by his evening with Ausable.

topics.title: Max, the midnight visitor, and the missile report
topics.ncert_sections: From the light switched on to Max's demand for the report

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how Max is described, how he entered the room and why his presence gives Fowler a real thrill.
Explain what the report is about and why rival agents want it.

topics.title: Ausable's balcony story and the knock at the door
topics.ncert_sections: From the complaint about the balcony to Max climbing over the window-sill

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how Ausable's detailed account makes the imaginary balcony convincing to Max.
Explain how Ausable uses the expected knock to frighten Max into leaving through the window.

topics.title: The twist ending and presence of mind
topics.ncert_sections: From Max's drop from the sill to 'there is no balcony'

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the surprise ending: the waiter at the door and the balcony that never existed.
Evaluate Ausable's presence of mind and the irony of an unarmed man defeating an armed spy.

topics.title: Vocabulary and language of the story

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the meanings of words from the chapter's glossary as used in the story.
Interpret descriptive expressions from the story and report its dialogue correctly.
